workstream: W-4 — Service-client principal check (I-3, addresses G6)
leg: third — re-execution under the Mission 2 reopen

base.note: The reopen's Wave 1 branch. The first two legs ran on hotfix/vacilando-ui-freshness-flash; this is the first W-4 run on a base carrying both the W-4 line and the Slice C public-tour line.

arrival_state.failing_test: W-4 · the ratchet > does not grow the advisory transitive-only set past its baseline of 3
arrival_state.assertion: expected 10 to be less than or equal to 3
arrival_state.why_it_was_not_caught_earlier: The numeric ceilings lived only in the vitest lock, never in prebuild. The check enforces list membership exactly in both directions, which stops a list growing WITHOUT an edit, but does not stop the edit itself. e7e585010 (2026-08-03) grew advisory_transitive_only 3 → 9 in a commit touching exactly one file — the allow-list — with next build staying green. 9187ae81a (2026-08-04) added the tenth. The breach stayed latent until the lock was run on a base containing both lines of work.

delta_reconciliation.unresolved_17_to_15: Not a fix. Two routes stopped IMPORTING a service client when Slice C moved it into guardTourActionRoute, so they left the enforced predicate and moved from `exceptions` to `advisory_transitive_only`.

fix.root_cause_addressed: Ceilings moved out of the lock and into the register (`ratchet` block in web/scripts/serviceClientPrincipal.allowlist.json), enforced by web/scripts/checkServiceClientPrincipal.mjs so a breach stops prebuild.

enforced_in_both_directions.under_ceiling: stale `ratchet-slack` — the floor dropped and nobody followed it down, which is the exact state that silently handed out 9 free exceptions between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-04
enforced_in_both_directions.absent: violation `ratchet-missing` — the bound cannot be deleted to make the build pass

fix.lock_assertion_strengthened: ceiling === live floor, replacing floor <= ceiling. Under the old assertion the 2026-08-04 slack was green; under the new one it is red the moment it appears.
fix.advisory_ceiling_raise_is_not_a_shrink: 3 → 10 ratifies a growth that already happened and was never bounded. Recorded with its cause in the register's ratchet.history.

at_the_cli_per_10_4.method: ceilings temporarily set to 24 / 3, `npm run check:service-client-principal` run as a command
at_the_cli_per_10_4.observed: 1 ratchet-exceeded breach + 1 ratchet-slack entry ('ceiling is 24 but the live floor is 15 — re-tighten it to 15, or it hands out 9 free exception(s)'), non-zero exit

locked_as_tests: FAILS when the allow-list is empty — the red state
FAILS on a stale entry, so the lists cannot accumulate residue
FAILS when a ceiling is left above a fallen floor — the slack state
FAILS when the count grows past a ceiling — the breach state
FAILS when no ceiling is recorded at all, so the count cannot be left unbounded

substantive_drift.claim_that_became_false: requiredActions is the route constant [view_tour_slots, view_tour_details] — so a decline- or cancel-only token cannot read context
substantive_drift.reality: REQUIRED_ACTIONS now lists all seven action kinds, including decline_tour and cancel_tour (:27-35)
substantive_drift.why: The widening is deliberate and argued in the route header (:18-25) — any credential on the same invitation may re-read what that invitation already disclosed to that same recipient — and authorizeTourAction still proves recipient binding, expiry and revocation. The defect is in the register, not the route.
substantive_drift.resolution: All four corrected in place and marked CORRECTED 2026-08-06, rather than rewritten to look as though they had always been right.

register_review.also_verified_this_run: requiredActions is a module-level constant in all seven public tour routes, never request-derived; guardTourActionRoute returns the service client only after authorizeTourAction succeeds (tourActionRouteGuard.ts:76, :89).

limits.unchanged_and_still_governing: The check proves a principal is RESOLVED, never that the result GATES the handler. W-14 and W-15 own that proof.

newly_evidenced_this_run.statement: W-4's enforced predicate is DIRECT IMPORT. A helper refactor is an exit from it: two routes left the enforced set with no change in their authority and landed on the weaker advisory list, bounded only by a count.
newly_evidenced_this_run.why_not: Rebuilding the predicate on reachability rather than import would change what the number means.
newly_evidenced_this_run.handed_to: W-15, as a named property to preserve

newly_evidenced_this_run.statement: The check enforces membership and now counts. Nothing binds a reason to the line it cites, so a reviewed exception can decay into an inaccurate one with the build green throughout — the exit criterion's 'reviewed artifact rather than a residue' eroding by a route the ratchet does not cover.
newly_evidenced_this_run.evidence_that_it_works: this run found 4 of 10 advisory reasons inaccurate, one of them substantively

note_on_scope: W-4 measures and freezes; it remediates nothing. No route's authority was changed by this leg.
